questions.stem: Why is sampling used in ecological studies?

options.text: Because scientists prefer to study only a few organisms
Because organisms can only be found in samples
Because sampling always gives exact results
Because it is impossible to count every organism in an area

questions.explanation: Sampling is used because it is impractical to count every organism in an area due to time, cost, and practical constraints. A representative sample provides a good estimate of the whole population without needing to survey everything.

options.text: A type of organism found in soil
A type of microscope
A graph showing population data
A square frame used to sample an area

questions.explanation: A quadrat is a square frame (commonly 0.25 m2 or 1 m2) placed on the ground to define a sampling area. Scientists count or estimate the organisms within the quadrat to gather data about species distribution and abundance.

options.text: Because it requires fewer quadrats
Because it makes the experiment faster
Because it ensures every position has an equal chance of being sampled, avoiding bias
Because it always gives the correct answer

questions.explanation: Random sampling is important because it avoids bias by ensuring every position in the sampling area has an equal chance of being selected. This makes the results representative of the whole area and allows valid statistical analysis.

options.text: A type of quadrat used in water
A method of counting animals by marking them
A random number generator
A line along which organisms are sampled at regular intervals

questions.explanation: A transect is a line (usually a tape measure) placed across a habitat along which organisms are sampled at regular intervals. Transects are useful for studying how species distribution changes across an environmental gradient.

questions.stem: How can you estimate the total population of a species in a field using quadrats?

options.text: Calculate the mean number per quadrat and multiply by the total number of quadrats that fit in the field
Weigh the organisms in each quadrat
Only count the organisms you can see from one spot
Count organisms in one quadrat and assume the rest of the field is the same

questions.explanation: To estimate total population, calculate the mean number of organisms per quadrat from several random samples, then multiply by the total number of quadrats that would fit in the entire field (total area / quadrat area).

options.text: The weight of organisms in a quadrat
The proportion of a quadrat area covered by a particular species
The number of individual organisms in a quadrat
The height of plants in a quadrat

questions.explanation: Percentage cover estimates the proportion of a quadrat area that is covered by a particular species. It is especially useful for plants that are difficult to count individually, such as grass or moss.

questions.stem: How can you make sampling results more reliable?

options.text: Choose the areas with the most organisms
Sample on a sunny day only
Use only one quadrat in the most interesting area
Use more quadrats and repeat the sampling

questions.explanation: Using more quadrats and repeating the sampling makes results more reliable. A larger sample size gives a more accurate representation of the whole area and allows calculation of more reliable mean values.
